_provenance.what: Hand-check of the low-overlap tail identified by code/rq1_audit/passage_overlap_audit.py, across BOTH test splits and independent of any model's performance on the item.
_provenance.annotator: second annotator (Claude, this session), single pass, no second rater, no kappa
_provenance.metric: share of question content words present in the passage, with singular/plural stemming
_provenance.sciq_coverage: census: every one of the 21 items with stemmed overlap < 0.40, plus a seeded 20-item sample of the 863 items >= 0.40
_provenance.obqa_coverage: seeded random sample of 25 of the 123 items at exactly 0.000 overlap

categories.topic_mismatch: the passage is about an unrelated subject; it cannot answer the question
categories.orthographic_defect: passage is on topic but a spelling/typo prevents lexical matching
categories.legitimate_low_overlap: passage is on topic and correct; low overlap is a property of the phrasing (paraphrase) or of the benchmark's design (deductive rule)

sample_above_0_40.note: 0/20 mismatched. A passage sharing >= 40% of a question's content words is structurally unlikely to be off-topic; both misses found above sit at 0.286 and 0.333, below that line.

detector_performance.recommended_operating_point: < 0.40 with a full census of the resulting ~21 items; the pool is small enough that precision does not matter.

obqa.interpretation: OpenBookQA's zero-overlap mass is entirely by design, not defect. `fact1` is a deductive one-clause rule and the question asks for an instance of it, so sharing no vocabulary is the intended relationship. Every sampled pair was a valid rule/instance link.

examples.245: fact 'a thermal insulator slows the transfer of heat' / question about a duck-feather jacket -- valid, zero shared vocabulary
examples.430: fact 'adding salt to a solid decreases the freezing point of that solid' / question about ice on a sidewalk -- valid
examples.480: fact 'a complete revolution of the Earth around the sun takes one solar year' / question 'what would occur once between January 1st and December 31st' -- valid
examples.255: fact 'alloys are made of two or more metals' / gold 'iron and carbon' -- on topic, though the fact is imprecise since carbon is not a metal. Counted as legitimate, flagged as a minor factual wobble rather than a pairing defect.
